parts.text: State what is meant by the ‘aim’ of a study.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Outline one aim of the study by Piliavin et al. (subway Samaritans).

text: The study by Canli et al. (brain scans and emotions) raised ethical issues of ‘right to withdraw’ and
‘protection from harm’.
Explain why the study by Canli et al. raised these ethical issues.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by ‘random allocation’, using this study as an example.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain one strength of using random allocation in this study.

text: In the study by Laney et al. (false memory), random allocation was used.
In the study by Bandura et al. (aggression), children were shown a room full of attractive toys to
play with but were told they were for other children.
Explain one of the two reasons Bandura et al. gave for doing this.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain which one of these investigations is a case study.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain one strength of using a case study to investigate this topic.

text: Two studies are using different methods to investigate the topic of dreaming in deaf people:
• Dr Kahlil is studying Joseph, who is deaf and has dreams about people using sign language.
• Dr Hart is studying six deaf people and six hearing people to compare the length of their REM
periods.
Describe positive correlations and negative correlations, using any examples.
Section B
Answer all questions in this section.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Jane has two possible ways to measure her dependent variable:
• by timing how quickly the participant can recall 10 nonsense words correctly
• by counting the number of spelling errors made when recalling 10 nonsense words.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Explain one strength of one of Jane’s measures of her dependent variable.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Explain one weakness of the measure of the dependent variable that you have referred
to in (a)(i).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Suggest one way that Jane can operationalise ‘speaking a language fluently’.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Jane used an independent measures design in her experiment.
Explain one reason why it would have been better for Jane to use a matched pairs design
than an independent measures design.

text: Jane is planning a laboratory experiment with two groups of participants. One group speaks one
language fluently and the other group speaks two or more languages fluently. Jane thinks this
may affect her dependent variable of how well they learn ‘nonsense’ words. These are words that
read like real words but have no meaning.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Explain why, at first, Kofi uses an unstructured observation.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
After watching different sports, Kofi can now use a structured observation.
Explain one strength of using a structured observation in Kofi’s study.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Kofi has decided to be a covert observer.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Suggest one strength of being a covert observer in this study.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Suggest one weakness of being a covert observer in this study.

text: Kofi is planning an observation of aggression in sport. He will attend a range of different sporting
events to record aggressive behaviour. At first, Kofi is not certain what kinds of behaviours he will
see.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest one open question Naia could ask about emotions.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Suggest one closed question Naia could ask about emotions.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Suggest one weakness of using a structured interview in Naia’s study.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
One participant says that Naia’s questions are too personal.
Explain two ethical guidelines that are important to overcome this problem.
Do not refer to protection from harm or right to withdraw in your answer.

Section C
Answer all questions in this section.

text: Naia wants to interview young people about how environmental issues make them feel. She
wants to collect data about emotional responses to issues such as recycling. She has decided to
conduct a structured interview.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe how Riley could conduct a natural experiment to investigate when the children are
nicer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Identify one practical weakness/limitation with the procedure you have described in your
answer to part (a) and suggest how your study might be done differently to overcome the
problem.
Do not refer to ethics or sampling in your answer.
